open_questions: Success rates vary widely across benchmarks (MLE-bench, MLAgentBench, MLRC-Bench) and agent designs, with no unified metric for "running correctly" versus "beating baselines".
Most results depend on specific scaffolding (AIDE, MLAB, R&D-Agent) and base models; generalization to other agent architectures is unclear.
Definitions of "beat baselines" differ: bronze medal, any medal, task success rate, gap closure percentage, relative improvement.
Contamination from pre-training data inflates performance on older tasks, while recent tasks show near-zero success.
Long-horizon reliability, error recovery, and autonomous iteration remain limited even for top agents.
Small models (7B) with RL training can match large proprietary models on some metrics, but absolute success rates are not always reported.
Scaling trends with compute budget, model size, and search strategies are not fully characterized across benchmarks.
